summary: Radar, 3 Nov 2026. I checked 8 items. Three are new and solid. (1) A JAMA Psychiatry survey (Nov 3) found 44% of drinkers on GLP-1 medicines say they drink less. It's emerging, and creators have covered it very little. (2) An observational AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 study of more than 250,000 adults with prediabetes and obesity found GLP-1 medicines were linked to 31% lower type 2 diabetes risk than metformin. It's rising, with Healthline and AJMC already covering it. (3) Lilly's indirect comparison of tirzepatide 15 mg with semaglutide 7.2 mg (Oct 29, about 4.5% more weight loss) gives us a 13:00 head-to-head Short in an obesity population. It must be labelled 'separate trials, not head-to-head'. The ObesityWeek REDEFINE 4 readout (CagriSema vs tirzepatide, Nov 14–17) is the next big head-to-head and needs its Short planned ahead of time. The Lane A queue still has the best long-form value: stopping, hair loss, fatigue, Thanksgiving (peaks Nov 18–27), birth control, injection site and dehydration. Recent hooks back each one: the Daily Maverick piece on stopping, Cleveland Clinic's surgery-after-GLP-1 news and cold/flu season. Body-worry Shorts are ready to go: three fracture studies show no extra fracture risk (Medscape, Nov 2) and a Bone meta-analysis came out Nov 2. Retatrutide gray-market seizures and a Cureus liver-injury case work only as one 'what's confirmed' Short (counts toward the gray-market cap of 1 a week). Rejected: compounding networks, online programs, Costa Rica 'research peptide' platforms and 'natural GLP-1 alternatives'. Not verified: the Cleveland Clinic surgery-after-GLP-1 paper (the Ann Surg title only appears in the signal feed) and whether TGA approved the Wegovy pill on Nov 3 (my search found only Aug–Oct reports, the newest saying it was still under evaluation).

candidates.topic: Will tirzepatide make me drink less? New JAMA Psychiatry survey: 44.2% of drinkers on GLP-1 medicines reported drinking less (54.1% among people screening positive for unhealthy drinking; 242 drinkers, RAND American Life Panel, Mar–Apr 2026)
candidates.angle: Calm 'Is this normal?' answer for people who notice wine tastes less appealing on a GLP-1. Self-reported perception only, class-level ('GLP-1 medicines', not tirzepatide-specific). Randomized trials are still underway, and GLP-1 medicines are not approved for alcohol use disorder. Mention that only 10% had heard of the link.
keywords: does Mounjaro make you drink less
why don't I want to drink on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Published Nov 3 in JAMA Psychiatry and picked up by Medical Xpress the same day. Holiday drinking season is starting. Few creator videos yet. Builds on the Medscape alcohol piece from our Oct 28 snapshot.

evidence.signal: Survey of 242 drinkers on GLP-1s: 44.2% reported drinking less, self-reported, not causal
Landscape of ongoing randomized incretin trials in psychiatry

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain weeks 36→88 on placebo), Metabolites regain systematic review (Oct 9), Daily Maverick 'Life after weight-loss medication' (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form redo. First sentence answers the title. Covers what the trial showed, why appetite returns and what helps keep results (protein, strength training, follow-up with your prescriber). Includes 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: ongoing; January spike when people review their medicines
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots with momentum rising (82→88). New mainstream 'life after' coverage. Employers dropping coverage pushes people to search about stopping (we use it only as context, never as a cost angle).

evidence.signal: Weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medicines
Mainstream 'what happens when the injections stop' feature

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide 7.2 mg: Lilly's indirect comparison (Oct 29) found about 4.5% more weight loss with tirzepatide 15 mg at 72 weeks in adults with obesity. Context: SURMOUNT-5, the only direct trial, which used semaglutide 2.4 mg
candidates.angle: 13:00 head-to-head Short, tirzepatide named first, obesity population. Say clearly 'separate trials, not head-to-head' and 'company-sponsored indirect comparison'. Contrast it with SURMOUNT-5 (tirzepatide 10/15 mg vs semaglutide 1.7/2.4 mg at maximum tolerated dose). Loop ending. Includes the don't-switch line.
keywords: which works better Zepbound or Wegovy
candidates.why_now: Lilly press release Oct 29, now in trade press (scanx Nov 3). Wegovy 7.2 mg was approved in March 2026, so people are searching the comparison. Tirzepatide-first obesity head-to-heads are our best 13:00 format (107–173 views).

evidence.signal: Indirect treatment comparison, tirzepatide 10/15 mg vs semaglutide 7.2 mg
Media pickup: '4.5% greater weight loss'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines vs metformin in prediabetes with obesity: AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 observational study of more than 250,000 adults. Linked to a 31% lower risk of type 2 diabetes, 1.5× the chance of blood sugar returning to normal, 15% fewer heart attacks and 20% fewer strokes
candidates.angle: 'Can tirzepatide stop prediabetes turning into diabetes?' Honest answer: this observational study (a conference presentation) links GLP-1 medicines to lower risk compared with metformin. Add SURMOUNT-1's 3-year prediabetes data as the randomized anchor. Explain who it's approved for and questions to bring to your doctor. 'Linked to', never 'prevents'. Put absolute rates next to the relative ones.
candidates.why_now: AHA newsroom release Nov 2. Healthline, AJMC, Cardiovascular Business and Medical Xpress picked it up within 24 h. Prediabetes is a core audience group with high search intent.

evidence.signal: More than 250,000 adults with prediabetes and obesity; observational; conference presentation
Mainstream trade pickup
Managed-care coverage of the same study

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: will it grow back? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026). The label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men, and 1.3% vs 0% on placebo. Refreshed by the Cureus semaglutide skin-side-effects meta-analysis of RCTs
candidates.angle: Verified Lane A long-form linked from both hair Shorts (the 1,016-view Short still feeds nothing). Shedding is 'particularly associated with' rapid weight loss, and 'no human studies show a direct effect on follicles'. Covers protein, patience and when to see a clinician.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots with momentum climbing. Our biggest Short ever is on this topic. New cutaneous-AE meta-analysis gives a fresh fact.

evidence.signal: Cutaneous adverse events with semaglutide, meta-analysis of RCTs

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slowly, alcohol and easing nausea. New angle: JAMA Psychiatry alcohol survey plus DOM digital-grocery-purchase study (Oct 29)
candidates.angle: Shorts and the 20:00 funnel to the live Thanksgiving and What to Eat long-forms. 'Is it normal to only manage half a plate?' Our own tips carry no source tag. No extreme-diet messaging.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots with steady acceleration. Seasonal peak is 2–3 weeks away, so publishing now gives us ranking time.

evidence.signal: Food purchases change during GLP-1-based treatment

candidates.topic: Retatrutide: what's confirmed? Phase 3 topline data (TRANSCEND-T2D-2) vs the unapproved 'research' products: FDA warnings, Malaysian seizures (RM341,000), UK border seizures of 'Godzilla' jabs, and a Cureus case of suspected liver injury after an unregulated product sold as retatrutide
candidates.angle: One 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Retatrutide is not approved anywhere, and online 'research' products are not the trial drug. Calm, no scare framing, never names sellers. Counts as the week's single gray-market Short.
candidates.why_now: Several independent seizure and regulatory stories within 48 h, plus a new case report. Retatrutide 'what's confirmed' Shorts are a proven top-tail format (207–276 views).
